question: With the KL anchor applied on-policy only (k1 in the reward, trained layouts T), does the drift the reward causes start in, and end up in, states the reference's human data rarely or never covered?
base: KL anchoring experiment 3 (architecture sweep, Claude desktop, 26 Oct 2026): arch_sweep.py vendored unchanged; same environment family, layout sets T/B/O, 300 demos per layout, RL 1500 updates x 64 episodes from the reference, lr 1e-3.

methods.k1rew: per-step reward r - beta*log(pi/pi_ref), anchor on RL's own samples only
methods.klonly: k1rew with task reward 0: optimum is the reference, so drift is optimizer noise through shared parameters

groups: states grouped by summed visits in the 300 human demos: T_high >= 200, T_mid 70-199, T_low 1-69; O_all = every valid state on the six unseen H=7 layouts (zero data)
measure: D_g(t) = mean TV(pi_t, pi_ref) over group g under k1rew minus the same under klonly (same unit and beta): reward-induced drift. Unit = (seed, eps); 16 units per architecture.

primary.H1_final_export: D_O(1500) - D_Thigh(1500) > 0 at beta 0.3: one-sided 95% t lower bound > 0 per network; supported if >= 3 of 4 networks (mlp64, mlp256, cnn, transformer).
primary.H2_onset: mean over t in {25, 50, 100} of D_O(t) - D_Thigh(t) > 0 at beta 0.3: same rule.
primary.H3_beta: export index E = (mean D_O - mean D_Thigh)/(mean D_O + mean D_Thigh) at 1500 is larger at beta 1.0 than 0.3: paired bootstrap over units (10,000), 5th percentile of the difference > 0 (resamples with a nonpositive denominator count against); same rule.

secondary.S1: replication of the original metric: raw TV ratio O_all / T_high under k1rew beta 0.3 > 1 (log, t lower bound > 0) per network
secondary.S2: raw log ratio under k1rew minus under klonly > 0: is the original metric's concentration reward-specific?
secondary.S3: D_Tlow(1500) - D_Thigh(1500) > 0: does reward-induced drift favour rare states within the trained layouts?

controls: tabular (no shared parameters): O drift must be exactly 0. none: descriptive.
development: Smoke 1 (seed 99, eps 0.01, mlp64 and transformer, k1rew/klonly beta 0.3) showed reference-visitation groups leave no rare trained states, so groups moved to human-demo counts. Smoke 2 (seeds 90-92, eps 0.01, tabular/mlp64/mlp256, all methods, counts cutoff 30) gave raw O/T ratios 0.7-2.0 under k1rew (the original metric replicates) but 0.7-3.8 under klonly, and reward-induced O minus T_high drift near 0 (-0.003, -0.002). The 30-visit cutoff put 90% of trained states in 'high', so cutoffs moved to 200/70 (quartiles). H1-H3 were written before smoke 2; S1-S3 were added after it. Smoke seeds are not reused (confirmation seeds 20-27).
